name: wasm_instruction_set

phase_0.boundary_condition: The validated module boundary that enforces type safety and prevents control flow from escaping defined regions.

⊢.justification: The state before any bytecode is parsed or memory is allocated, representing the void from which the module genesis begins.

⊣.justification: The closed boundary of a fully validated WebAssembly module where all types are resolved and control flow is contained.

≻.justification: The forward morphism where operations consume operands and push results onto the operand stack, driving execution forward.

≺.justification: The reverse morphism where operations consume values from the stack, descending the data structure to retrieve operands.

⋈.justification: The composition of individual instructions into a linear sequence that forms the body of a function or block.

⊙.justification: The identity element where a local variable holds its own value, acting as a self-referential storage slot within the function scope.

∈.justification: The control flow split where a conditional instruction branches execution into two distinct paths: the then-arm and the else-arm.

∋.justification: The reconstitution point where divergent control flow paths (then/else or loop iterations) merge back into a single execution stream.

⊤.justification: The affirmative state where a conditional evaluates to true, activating the forward execution path of the branch.

⊥.justification: The negative state where a conditional evaluates to false, activating the alternative or skip path of the branch.

⊞.justification: The paradice state where a switch-like instruction holds multiple potential targets simultaneously until the runtime index resolves the specific path.

◻.justification: The irreversible fixation of data into linear memory, creating a permanent record of the value at a specific address.

phase_3.void_description: The state of a module before instantiation where no memory is allocated and no stack exists.
phase_3.true_description: A validated execution path where all type checks pass and the stack depth remains non-negative.
phase_3.false_description: A failed execution path where a trap occurs due to type mismatch, division by zero, or out-of-bounds memory access.
phase_3.both_description: A state where a br_table instruction holds multiple potential targets simultaneously before the runtime index resolves the specific branch.

steps.domain_action: Initialize the module state as void before any bytecode is processed.
Chain the initial sequence of instructions to form the function prologue.
Push the initial arguments onto the operand stack.
Allocate local variables as identity slots for temporary storage.
Open a conditional block based on a runtime comparison.
Execute the then-arm when the condition is true.
Push intermediate results within the then-arm.
Chain arithmetic operations within the then-arm.
Merge the then-arm back to the common exit point if no else exists.
Open a nested conditional block for complex logic.
Execute the inner then-arm.
Execute the inner else-arm when the condition is false.
Pop values from the stack to prepare for the next operation.
Rejoin the inner conditional paths at the inner block end.
Enter a br_table state holding multiple potential jump targets.
Compute the index value to select the target.
Resolve the br_table to a single target and merge control flow.
Chain the post-branch instructions.
Store the final result into linear memory.
Pop the result from the stack for return.
Close the function and return to the module boundary.

phase_5.compiler_frontend: wasm-opt or binaryen which translates high-level code into WebAssembly bytecode.
phase_5.ipc_mechanism: The operand stack which mediates data flow between instructions.
phase_5.memory_mechanism: Linear memory, a contiguous byte array accessed via load and store instructions.
phase_5.scheduler_mechanism: The structured control flow graph which dictates the order of instruction execution.
phase_5.alfs_store: The WebAssembly specification which defines the canonical instruction set and validation rules.

phase_6.cycle_cost: CPU cycles consumed per instruction execution and memory bandwidth for load/store operations.
phase_6.pre_cycle_state: The operand stack contains input values and the linear memory holds initial state.
phase_6.post_cycle_state: The operand stack contains the result value and linear memory holds updated state.
phase_6.delta_s_verdict: ΔS ≈ 0 — The deterministic nature of WebAssembly execution ensures that the information content is preserved through reversible stack operations and fixed memory writes.
